scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

F-01.statement: Dispute ticket response times: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, within the 3.0-day SLA, across 2440 tickets.

F-03.statement: Manual read route completion for 9200 accounts was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over 2026-08..09.

F-04.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 with ESTIMATED reads, 1785 with ACTUAL reads (3025 total).

F-05.statement: Billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records, indicating no recorded tariff changes.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, to be executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-08.statement: route-log identifies 14 distinct lagging routes with varying completion rates; sample record shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP.statement: Dispute tickets doubled because Customer Service lacks capacity/tools to answer tickets fast, and an AI auto-answer/auto-fix agent would resolve the surge.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic billing errors (e.g. mis-handling of estimates or read types), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-DEGRADATION.statement: AMI register read delivery via the MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded or failed starting August, forcing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-PROCESS-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter-read collection or the daily upload handoff (H-FIELD-BILL) from the contracted field vendor broke down since August, causing missing reads and estimate substitution leading to disputes.

H-GENUINE-BILLING-ERRORS-NOT-R.statement: The ticket surge reflects a real increase in incorrect bills requiring manual billing-operations adjustments (per K-BILLWRITE authority), not a lack of fast/automated responses.

interpretation_history.interpretation: CRM data (E-01) shows dispute response times — median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days — sit within the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets. Response handling speed/capacity is not degraded, so the ticket surge is not explained by a response-speed/capacity gap.

CRM dispute volume by month (E-02) shows roughly stable ticket counts of 610 and 590 in June-July 2026, then jumping to 1180 in August and 1260 in September — confirming the magnitude and August onset of the surge referenced in the initial request, but revealing nothing about its cause.

Route-log data (E-03) shows manual meter-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 manual-read accounts over 2026-08..09, i.e. a measurable shortfall in field read collection during the dispute-surge period. This does not by itself show the shortfall caused the bill disputes, but it is consistent with missed manual reads forcing estimate substitution.

Billing-db (E-04) shows disputed bills split by read type: 1240 with ESTIMATED reads vs 1785 with ACTUAL reads (3025 total). ACTUAL-read bills form the majority (59%) of disputes, so missing-read/estimate-substitution causes can explain only a minority of the surge; most disputed bills had a real meter read on file.

Billing-db's tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes are recorded in the system of record. This rules out a tariff/rate change as a cause of the bill disputes, but does not speak to AMI delivery, manual-read process, or import validation rule causes.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's stakeholder claim that there has been no tariff change this year reiterates, as an unverified claim, the same conclusion already established authoritatively by E-05 (billing-db tariff_change_log, 0 records). It adds no new information and does not speak to AMI delivery, manual-read process, or import validation rule causes.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative, incomplete) claims the field team has been short three readers since July, causing manual-read routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills. This is an unverified causal explanation offered for the route-completion shortfall already observed in E-03, by a stakeholder with a stated bias toward attributing problems to staffing and an incentive to gain contract headcount.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This document (E-08) establishes the contractual basis for route priority change requests: the utility may request them, but execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager. It governs authority over the push_route_update protected action and does not speak to the dispute-surge root cause.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

It confirms variation across routes but says nothing about why these routes lag (staffing vs. other field-process factors).

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and automatically fix whatever is causing wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180 (Aug) / 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-02).
59% of disputed Aug-Sep bills (1785 of 3025) carried ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED substitutes (E-04).
Manual-read route completion fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts over Aug-Sep (E-03).
Dispute response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d/p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA, E-01), ruling out slow response as the symptom's driver.
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute tickets doubled from ~600/month to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-02), despite response times staying within SLA (median 1.6d/p90 2.8d vs 3.0d, E-01) and no recorded tariff change (E-05), while 59% of disputed bills carried ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED substitutes (E-04). This pattern indicates the billing import + validation step itself is generating incorrect bills regardless of read availability, driving the surge, rather than a response-capacity gap or missing-read estimate substitution being the dominant cause.
